content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, matches the original on randomized inputs in your range, and the bundle is much smaller.

**Results**

| Check | Original (lodash) | Migrated (es-toolkit) |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run size -- …` (min+gzip) | 9054 bytes | 606 bytes |
| Own code in bundle | 177 bytes | 95 bytes |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json` | — | passes |
| Equivalence | — | 25,013 randomized cases pass |

The equivalence test compared `byId` (including key order), `totalAge`, and `isBlank` against the original. It covered empty arrays, duplicate ids, and the `isBlank` value kinds in your range, including `{length: n}` objects. The test lives in the scratchpad, so the project only has the new `out/module.ts`.

**What changed**

- `keyBy` comes from `es-toolkit/array`. The `(row) => row.id` iteratee gives the same string keys and last-wins behaviour as lodash.
- `sumBy` comes from `es-toolkit/math`. The `'age'` shorthand became `(row) => row.age`. Both return `0` for an empty array.
- `isEmpty` comes from `es-toolkit/compat`. The strict package has no `isEmpty`, so this is the only library option. Its `isEmpty(value?: any)` overload accepts `unknown`, so no adapter was needed.
- Exported names and signatures are unchanged, including `Row`, `Config`, `byId`, `totalAge` and `isBlank`.

Nothing was installed. The existing `node_modules` (es-toolkit 1.53.2, lodash 4.18.1) was used as is.
